role: Local Codex Session Recovery Specialist and Academic Research Provenance Auditor
task: Recover and preserve the authentic OpenAI Codex interaction transcripts generated through Visual Studio Code during the development of Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 of the DS675 Machine Learning Mini-Project.

project.working_environment: Visual Studio Code with the OpenAI Codex extension

objective: Recover the complete available record of Codex instructions, responses, tool executions, code-generation requests, corrections, and technical discussions associated with preparing the two milestones.

requirements: Do not modify the DS675 project source code.
Do not modify or delete original Codex session files.
Do not alter Git history, branches, or commits.
Do not clear caches, reset the Codex extension, or reinstall software.
Do not upload recovered transcripts to GitHub.
Do not send private transcript data to external services.
Use local parsing and file inspection whenever possible.
Do not expose authentication tokens or secrets in terminal output.
Request authorization before accessing directories outside the permitted user-owned Codex and project locations.
Create archive files only in an explicitly designated private output directory.

additional_checks: Inspect Codex session history available through the Visual Studio Code extension.
Inspect the configured Codex data directory.
Identify whether the sessions were created in Windows, WSL, a remote environment, or a development container.
Check accessible archived sessions and legitimate user-created local backups.
Use available session metadata or state indexes to identify sessions not currently visible in the extension UI.
Check alternate Codex homes only when their locations are known or explicitly authorized.
Account for session files stored as plain JSONL or supported compressed rollout formats.
Do not assume that the extension displays every locally retained session.
Do not assume that every session related to the project has the same working directory.
search_strategy: Find candidate sessions using session timestamps, working directories, repository paths, titles, and session identifiers.
Search user messages and recorded commands for DS675-related keywords.
Use the repository's Git history to identify relevant dates and operations, without treating Git as a substitute for conversation records.
Inspect sessions associated with the preparation of Milestone 1 and Milestone 2, including work completed before the public repository was created.
Include related sessions even when a temporary workspace or alternate working directory was used.
Inspect available archived and resumed sessions.

transcript_recovery.source_of_truth: Original locally retained Codex session records.
requirements: Identify the original session files associated with the project.
Preserve complete original session files in a private evidence archive.
Retain original timestamps, session identifiers, source environment, and working-directory metadata.
Retain available user prompts and Codex assistant responses.
Retain available tool-call records, commands, execution results, errors, and technical feedback.
Retain relevant references to files inspected or modified.
Include resumed sessions and linked sessions when they contribute to either milestone.
Do not merge distinct sessions into a fabricated continuous conversation.
Do not replace original transcripts with descriptions generated from Git commits.
Do not claim unavailable records or hidden internal reasoning were recovered.
Mark truncated, missing, inaccessible, or malformed records clearly.
Do not silently discard failed operations, rejected suggestions, or student-requested corrections.
human_readable_conversion: Convert available interaction events into a chronological Markdown transcript.
Keep original user and assistant message text verbatim.
Label tool commands and outputs distinctly from conversational messages.
Preserve the original sequence of events.
Include timestamps and event identifiers where available.
Represent non-text events through faithful metadata references.
Do not invent attachment contents or unrecorded outputs.
Do not add summaries inside the transcript body.

milestone_2: Selection of Area C and n1.
Review of the six selected studies.
milestone_classification.important: Classify sessions using the recorded task and actual content, not simply the repository name or commit date.

student_ai_interaction_analysis.purpose: Create a factual evidence map showing how the student instructed, directed, reviewed, and corrected Codex work.
categories: Student approval, rejection, or modification of proposed results.
integrity_rules: Use only actions documented in the recovered sessions.
Do not attribute Codex-generated implementation to manual student coding.
Do not attribute research decisions to Codex when the student demonstrably provided them.
Do not attribute research decisions to the student without supporting records or separate clearly labeled testimony.
Differentiate student requests, AI recommendations, executed operations, and verified outcomes.
Record decisions only when the session contains evidence of those decisions.
Do not infer that the student reviewed or understood an output merely because it was generated.

instructions: Read relevant Git history without changing it.
Identify commits whose dates, files, or messages correspond to recovered Codex sessions.
Associate sessions with commits only when timestamps, file changes, or explicit session records support the connection.
Distinguish work performed before repository creation from later reproducibility packaging.
Do not use a commit as proof that the student manually wrote the code.
Do not fabricate missing interaction records from commit messages.
Do not exclude relevant sessions simply because their changes were never committed.

output.storage: Private local directory outside the public DS675 repository.

structure.original_sessions/: Exact preserved copies of relevant original Codex session records.
structure.session_index.csv: Session identifier, timestamp range, original path, working directory, milestone, and completeness status.
structure.contribution_evidence.csv: Student instruction or decision, supporting session, event identifier, timestamp, and evidence locator.
structure.git_session_mapping.csv: Evidence-based links between Codex sessions and relevant Git commits.
structure.recovery_report.md: Discovery methods, total sessions recovered, missing records, and known limitations.
structure.integrity_manifest.json: SHA-256 hashes and metadata for original session files and transcript exports.

transcript_formats: Original JSONL or original retained session format.

validation: Verify all original files remain unchanged.
Calculate checksums for preserved session records.
Check event order and timestamp consistency.
Avoid duplicate sessions and duplicated conversation events.
Verify that every transcript has a source file.
Check that any conversion preserves the available textual messages.
Identify sessions with missing tool output or incomplete event data.
Distinguish complete recovered sessions from partial recoveries.
Report any relevant data that could not be recovered.
privacy_and_academic_submission: Keep the complete original archive private.
Do not commit transcripts or session databases into the public repository.
Session files may contain sensitive paths, credentials, environment variables, or unrelated work.
Identify sensitive content without changing the original evidence.
Prepare a separate review copy only when necessary.
Log every redaction in any derivative copy.
Use an NJIT-approved private submission channel for academic disclosure.
Do not use redaction to hide substantive AI assistance or student instructions.
If the professor requires complete transcripts, provide the authentic records securely and clarify any privacy concerns directly.
final_instruction: Recover authentic Codex interaction evidence, not a reconstructed narrative. Preserve the available original instructions, responses, commands, and outcomes associated with both milestones. Operate read-only on the original sources, maintain a verifiable chain of provenance, and report all limitations honestly. Never claim complete recovery unless the accessible records support that conclusion.
